log.content: Timber, tar, and bilge. You are on your back in a chalk circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship; the deck is already moving. Three sailors stare as if they stole a rite and it worked. The Crown does not know yet. A knife is offered hilt-first if you nod — not in your hand until you do.

log.content: Accept the offer

Jax said yes to the smugglers, and the deal was done right there. The smugglers passed over a knife, a oilskin, and a paper slip for a bunk in the crew tier. A soft blue window opened behind Jax's eyes and listed the new things Jax owned. The smugglers said the Circle takes its cut on the first run, and then stepped back.

log.content: Look around this arrival

Jax turned a slow circle on the spot and looked over the whole hold of the grain-ship, counting what was really there. The smugglers watched Jax look without saying a word, and one of them shifted a crate to block a stack of sacks. Beyond the crates, a low door sits in the hull with a bar across it and a lantern hung above.

log.content: Say something…

Jax asked the nearest of the smugglers straight out where they were, and the question hung in the close air of a harbor circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship. The smugglers said, "You're in the hold of a grain-ship out of Valespire harbor, and the Circle runs this one, so mind your asking." The one who had passed the knife looked at the door in the hull before he said it. Past the crates, the low door in the hull still has its iron bar across it, and the bar is not locked.

log.content: Do something else…

Jax turned away from the talk and set both hands flat on the grain sacks, pushing until the stack shifted and settled against the hull with a soft rush of seed. Behind them smugglers went quiet all at once, and one of them stepped forward so that the deck boards creaked. The gap Jax had opened showed a second row of sacks stacked tight against the low door in the hull, and the iron bar across that door stood clear in the lamplight.

log.content: Say something…

Jax lifted their chin toward the smugglers and asked outright where this grain-ship was taking them. The smugglers said, "Down the harbor circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship, past the last of the sacks. Then out through the harbor gate. That's all we say for now." The smuggler who spoke folded their arms and did not look away from Jax. A barge chain rattles loose on the other side of the hull, and a thin line of daylight grows along the top of the low door.

log.content: Look around this arrival

Jax turned slowly on their heels and looked over the whole of a harbor circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship from the sacks at the near wall to the dark ribs of the hull above. The smugglers did not move to stop them, and one of them watched as if they had seen a newcomer look around many times before. Behind the lower row of sacks, a narrow gap showed a second row stacked tight against the hull, and a rope hung down there with a hook at its end.

log.content: Travel toward Cathedral Close

Jax had spent the dark hours on the harbor edge of Cathedral Close, sleeping rough where the grain-ship left them. Jax put one foot in front of the other along the back streets and set out for Cathedral Close, still wearing their clothes and carrying nothing else in their bare hands. The morning light came up grey over the rooftops and the stones underfoot changed from wet to dry as the streets climbed. Ahead, the tall stone towers of Cathedral Close rose above the low roofs, and a thin bell began to ring somewhere behind them.

log.content: Walk on

Jax stood in the open courtyard of Cathedral Close, where the cathedral shadow cut a long grey band across the cobbles. Jax walked the length of the close and let their eyes move over the kitchens, the doors, and the people working there. Nell Rudd looked up from a crate of turnips and nodded at Jax without stopping her hands. Col Thatch stacked firewood against the wall and watched Jax pass, cheerful and still. A door in the north wall of the close stood open, and warm bread smell came out of it.

log.content: Analyze Nell Rudd

Jax kept their hands loose at their sides and watched Nell Rudd from across the courtyard, counting the small things she did without deciding to. Nell set a turnip down and turned the crate so the broken slat faced the wall, and her eyes found Jax a half-breath before she spoke. She wiped her palms on her apron and waited, and beside her @:8 stacked wood without once looking at Jax.

log.content: Talk to Nell Rudd

Jax crossed the close to the crate where Nell Rudd stood and stopped a step short of her. "The people who do the hard work deserve someone standing up for them, and I mean to be that someone," Nell Rudd said. Jax was a new face, and she didn't trade words with new faces for free—he could buy a turnip or tell her what he wanted first. Col Thatch set the last of the firewood against the north wall and leaned on the stack to watch, arms crossed and face easy.

log.content: Travel toward Cathedral Undercroft

Jax left the crowded stones of Cathedral Close behind and walked the narrow back streets between tall, damp walls. Jax kept to the shadowed side of the lane and headed for Cathedral Undercroft, stepping over a shallow gutter of standing water. A door banged shut somewhere above. A dog barked once and then went quiet. Ahead, a steep stone stair disappears down under a low arch where the ground smells cold and wet.
systemLog: Travel: back streets between Cathedral Close and Cathedral Undercroft — leg 1 of 2 — +30 min, now morning; Cathedral Undercroft still ahead; quiet stretch, nobody met on the road

log.content: Walk on

Jax stood on the worn stone floor of Cathedral Undercroft, deep under the street they had left. They took one step forward into the quiet hall, letting the sound of their own feet tell them how large the room was. The Undercroft answered with a long, low echo that rolled away down a corridor and did not come back. A row of stone pillars marched off into the dark ahead of them, and somewhere past the pillars a single lamp burned.

log.content: Look around this arrival

Jax turned a slow circle on the stone floor of Cathedral Undercroft and looked at what the dark had been keeping from them. Their eyes found that the pillars were not bare and that small pale roots pushed up between the flagstones along the wall. High above, thin cracks let down lines of pale daylight from the Valespire streets, and dust turned slowly in those beams. Far down the hall a single lit lamp hung from the last pillar, and something metal on the floor below it gave back a soft yellow shine.

log.content: Travel toward Contract Hall

Jax came up out of Cathedral Undercroft and into a narrow back street where the stone walls stood close on both sides. Jax kept to the shaded edge of the street and walked on toward Contract Hall, one steady step after another past the high walls. The street stayed quiet, and the only sound was the scrape of Jax's own feet on the worn paving. Ahead, the roofs of Contract Hall stood above the lane, with a single high window throwing out a sheet of pale daylight.

log.content: Walk on

Jax stepped off the street and into Contract Hall, and the noise of the midday crowd fell away behind them. Jax crossed the floorboards to the notice-board and stopped in front of the rows of Crown job postings pinned there. Hobb Barrow looked up from a long sheet of paper and watched Jax the whole way across the room without saying a word. Near the wall, Osric Marl kept his hands folded and his eyes down, but his head turned a little toward the board. A small wooden plaque on the wall by the board reads Cathedral Undercroft in careful letters, and one crown seal hangs beside it on a red cord.

log.content: Talk to Hobb Barrow

Jax crossed the floor of Contract Hall and stopped across the long sheet of paper from Hobb Barrow. Hobb said, "You walked in here and looked at me like you already know my name. So say it, or ask what you came to ask." Jax asked what the paper was for, and Hobb set one hand flat on it and did not answer at once. Hobb said, "It is a list of the ones who never came back from the undercroft. I keep it because someone has to. Do you want to help me with it, or not?"

log.content: Travel toward Lowmarket

Jax came out of Contract Hall and turned onto the back streets, in the same clothes they had walked in with. Jax set off toward Lowmarket, one foot in front of the other, and the crowd of the hall stayed behind them. The narrow street gave back only the sound of Jax's own steps and a cart creaking somewhere out of sight. A chipped painted sign hung over the next corner, and two women carried a basket of onions past a stack of empty barrels.

log.content: Walk on

Lowmarket is a long row of stalls built from old wood and torn sails, and the noise of it rolls over Jax from both sides. Jax keeps walking between the stalls until the crowd thins near a stack of rusted metal drums, then stops and lets the pack slide off their shoulder to the ground. Maud Pike watches them from behind a folding table of small brass parts and says nothing, and a few paces on Idra Dunmore counts coin into a tin without looking up. A narrow aisle opens past the drums toward the back of the market, where a canvas awning flaps loose in the wind off the west wall.

log.content: Do something else…

Jax stepped away from the brass parts and moved along the aisle behind the drums, putting the whole length of two stalls between them and the two women. Maud Pike watched them go without saying a word, her hands still over the tray of little brass parts. Idra Dunmore turned to follow Jax with her eyes alone, flat and patient, the way a person waits for a debt to come due. Ahead of Jax the back of the market narrowed into a dim gap between two sailcloth stalls, and warm air came out of it smelling of old rope and cooking oil.

lorebook.name: The Sevenfold Circle
lorebook.summary: Seven brass rings inlaid in cathedral stone. Each ring is a vow: Name, Origin, Flesh, Gift, War, Court, Scale. The seventh — Scale — stuttered. That stutter is why two stamps exist. Standing on the circle after arrival still tingles. Leaving it is allowed. Returning later may re-roll a glitched blessing, at a cost the System will not preview.

lorebook.name: Pactborn and Calamity Mark
lorebook.summary: The System stamps summoned souls. [Pactborn] is the public hero class the court paid for: visible quest markers from the Crown, easier lodging, harder persuasion when you try to leave. [Calamity Mark] is the failure state in their doctrine: shops close, priests ward you, the Ash Court can find you. A soul may show one stamp on the panel and the other in rumor. Appraisal of the person (not just items) can reveal the true mix.

lorebook.name: Circle Blessing (Unidentified)
lorebook.summary: When registration completes or Appraisal fires in play, the System may grant one glitched passive via <item-gain> — never pre-seeded on New Game. Until Appraised it is [???]. Possible truths (pick one per campaign, do not list them in play): a once-per-day rewind of a single failed check; speech that people hear as the language they trust; a weapon that only exists while they are angry; a mark that beasts will not strike first; a leak that lets Ash Court scouts hear their location. Naming it without Appraisal is a lie. Power fantasy without a cost is forbidden — the glitch always has a tell.

lorebook.name: Pellane and Valespire
lorebook.summary: Pellane is a highland kingdom. Valespire is its capital: cathedral, palace, Lowmarket, west wall, The Weighing Cup, Contract Hall, Cathedral Undercroft. They are losing a grinding war against the Ash Court — not cartoon demons, a rival polity that uses ember-wards and bargains. The court told the public that a summoned Pactborn will end the war in a season. That is propaganda.

lorebook.name: The Ash Court
lorebook.summary: A coalition of ember-priests and march-lords east of the Cinderflow. They call Pellane oath-breakers. They will recruit a Calamity Mark as proof the Scale rejected Pellane. They are not mindless evil. Individual envoys can be honorable, cruel, or both.

lorebook.name: The Scale
lorebook.summary: Pellane’s state divinity is The Scale — balance, contracts, weighed souls. Priests insist summoning is holy. Street rumor says The Scale only watches. The System never confirms gods. Treat The Scale as culture unless a special seed makes it act.

lorebook.name: Appraisal Law
lorebook.summary: Reading items, people, and places requires the Appraisal skill or a licensed Appraiser. Unlicensed Appraisal in Valespire is a fine. Offer Appraisal as a choice or a hire, not as omniscience.

lorebook.name: The Other Summoned
lorebook.summary: Every successful Sevenfold ritual in recorded Pellane history pulled two souls and only advertised one. The other is hidden, exiled, or working for the Ash Court. This age’s other summoned is alive. They are a person with Earth clothes too — not a boss statue.

lorebook.name: The Weighing Cup
lorebook.summary: A cathedral-close inn. Stew, beds, and rumor. Keep it a generic hub.

lorebook.name: Valespire Contract Hall
lorebook.summary: The city’s job board and rank desk. Posted contracts, politics, and a clerk who cares more about stamps than people. Guild pressure is social, not a forced party.

lorebook.name: Cathedral Undercroft
lorebook.summary: Numbered dungeon floors under the cathedral. Visited rooms are known; the rest are outline and fog. First Blood rules: describe the room before any creature. The court may send a Pactborn here as a morale show. A field chirurgeon class still has to fight on these floors.

before.campaignPremise:
The Summoned Pact: You were an ordinary person on Earth. A ritual in another world — the Sevenfold Circle, under Valespire Cathedral — pulled you through. The kingdom of Pellane summoned a [Pactborn] to end a war with the Ash Court. The System also rolled a second stamp: [Calamity Mark]. One summoned soul can carry either, or flicker between them. The court will call you Hero. The Ash Court will call you theirs. You do not have to answer either.

LOCATION LANGUAGE (BINDING): Camera is HERE — the seeded summon place for this run (cathedral circle, war camp, cell, arena, shrine, festival square, Ash-adjacent ritual hall, treaty tent, harbor hold, ruined west-wall circle, infirmary, or a locked alone-arrival ruin: barn, bathhouse, watchtower stump, market hall, foundation outline, burnt waystation). Alone-arrival cards: no summoners on page one; the building noun is already locked by the card. Do not teleport them to the Sevenfold Circle if Location is already somewhere else. Never call this interior "a nearby building." "The court" is Pellane's Crown / the people in this room, not the enemy. The enemy polity is the Ash Court. Do not use "the court" as both current room and the enemy in the same beat.

ORIGINALITY (BINDING): Never name published novels, anime, or games in play. Never import unique skill names, distinctive places, or plots from any series. Inn, guild, and dungeon are generic hubs with SynapticGM names only.

GENRE PALETTE (ORIGINAL NAMES — use these):
- System screens and classes are in-world. A blue panel is private and earned after the scene; code owns numbers. Classes exist (handler, field chirurgeon, wall-warden, unmarked). A healer class may still fight — that is a job, not a copied protagonist.
- Hero-summon gone wrong / villain-summon: [Pactborn] vs [Calamity Mark]. Player choice. No forced allegiance.
- Earth origin: clothes and pockets. Permanent displacement. No logout button, no VR-helmet plot.
- Inn hub: The Weighing Cup, a cathedral-close common room (beds, rumor, stew).
- Guild hub: Valespire Contract Hall (posted jobs, rank boards, politics).
- Dungeon: Cathedral Undercroft — numbered floors; fog on unvisited rooms. Street map stays o

openingEstablishment.pickedHook:
Location: a harbor circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship
Who is here / who summoned: Smugglers who stole a Scale rite and panicked when it worked
Why this happened: They wanted luck for a cargo run. They pulled an Earth soul. The Crown does not know yet.
Opening offer (optional — player may refuse): Keep their secret and they will kit you as crew (knife, oilskin, a bunk). Shout for the Crown and you keep Earth kit — and they may dump you at the quay.
- Timber, tar, a chalk circle in a ship’s hold. The boat is moving.
- A blue panel hangs. Someone swears. Someone laughs once and stops.
- A sailor’s knife is offered hilt-first if you nod.
openingEstablishment.pickedHookFallback: Timber, tar, and bilge. You are on your back in a chalk circle in the hold of a Valespire grain-ship; the deck is already moving. A blue panel hangs over stacked sacks. Three sailors stare as if they stole a rite and it worked. The Crown does not know yet. A knife is offered hilt-first if you nod — not in your hand until you do.
